answer: Neighbor-overlap routing quota. Each edge is admitted only if the source reaches k disjoint relay paths whose terminal neighborhoods overlap the established graph by at least t distinct agents over a rolling window. A cluster sharing one juniper gateway collapses to a single neighborhood. Reusing an umber relay pool fails diversity checks. An attacker can rent tundra hosts, but every identity must provision distinct external paths and maintain them; shared neighbors are rejected, so cost scales with unique network vantage points and relay upkeep.
